findings.title: Acquired raw ECH tasks escape exceptional caller ownership
findings.cause: Negotiated raw top-level and parallel Vec JoinHandles detach when preparation/request/await returns early or bounded future is cancelled. Exact Origin has no guard for parent/serving tasks. QuicOrigin has no guard and its optional TCP listener plus TCP connection tasks are raw/unregistered. Sender Drop can signal a parent waiting in select; it does not interrupt current handshake awaits or own TCP descendants.
findings.remedy: Prepare before acquisition; eagerly own real peers with existing ConnectionPeer where contracts fit, and concrete lexical child ownership for actual multi-connection origins. Drop must stop/abort every owned task/endpoint; explicit returned failures must finitely drain outcomes. Do not introduce a global task framework.
findings.regression: At each distinct canonical owner seam, complete real handshake/request/response or actual GET readiness, retain Client/socket/runtime externally, cancel owner before next accept/serving completion, observe actual peer destruction/socket release before finite backup. Parallel acquisition/first-child failure must observe all started children; include unchanged success positives.
findings.limits: Source-supported detach contract only; no host leak measured, no indefinite resource leak claimed. Sender closure can cooperatively stop a parent. Drop cancellation is not an awaited join.

findings.title: Normal and error finish discard completed serving and protocol failures
findings.cause: Exact/H3 parents abort/drop serving handles without awaiting their completed TestResults; H3 TCP descendants detach and return unit while ignoring handshake/head/write/shutdown failures. Exact H2 accept drain loops match only Some(Ok), swallowing any terminal H2 error; H1 WebSocket read_to_end explicitly ignores its result. Negotiated sequential await?? and completed request result? loops can discard other already-completed failures.
findings.remedy: Retain completed child results, abort and finitely join live children on failure, and combine original primary/secondary typed causes using current concrete fixture facilities. Distinguish actual expected shutdown/disconnect/rejection from unrelated protocol/I/O error; do not replace broad swallowing with blanket suppression.
findings.regression: Drive actual GET/opening and healthy response first, then inject distinct typed completed failures into two real canonical children or drive actual H2/WS read fault. Require original types/backend get_io and context survive explicit finish, and sibling destruction precedes return; use positive deliberate disconnect and normal completion controls. No copied serving implementation.
findings.limits: Existing response/ECH assertions do not establish late child or shutdown error health. Actual H2 I/O source inspection supports a causal read-fault test, but its reachable fault setup still needs implementation review/native proof. Existing shared A106 owner repair remains closed.

findings.title: Fixture bounds replace actual Elapsed with strings
findings.cause: Outer deadline mappings discard Elapsed. H3 finish count waits also discard it in formatted count messages. Existing contexts are useful and must survive alongside the concrete cause.
findings.remedy: Use existing compatible PeerDeadline where its context fits, or one concrete owner-local contextual error holding Elapsed. Keep all existing periods and messages; ensure acquired tasks still take owned cleanup on expiry.
findings.regression: Poll the actual canonical bounded path under entered paused time with a pending future; require typed Elapsed through source plus literal original context, inner typed error and immediate ready positives. Count-wait expiry should retain actual Elapsed as well as count context. Test-util is enabled; no bound increase.
findings.related: New owner scope of the established typed-deadline pattern; do not imply existing A104/A125/A162 repairs regressed.

findings.title: No-direct-DNS route control assumes fixed port9 is refused
findings.cause: Nothing in the test owns or checks127.0.0.1:9. Another listener/service can accept the proxy connection; the comment does not establish refusal.8443 likewise is an ambient origin port though intended to be unreachable through refused proxy.
findings.remedy: Use held testkit tcp::ReservedPort ephemeral address for all refusal routes, preserving Proxy category and zero DNS queries. Its macOS release/rebind limitation is documented and remains qualified.
findings.regression: Retain positive actual direct discovery/DNS exchange and existing successful proxy no-ECH tests; verify selected refusal address remains the reserved handle and all three route categories stay Proxy. This is fixture input isolation, not production DNS evidence. No need to test a duplicate of ReservedPort implementation.

findings.title: QUIC owner acquisition changes local-address error to port0
findings.cause: endpoint.local_addr().map_or(0,...) silently replaces an actual I/O failure with a valid-shaped zero port, so later request setup can obscure the acquisition cause.
findings.remedy: Resolve address fallibly before spawning TCP/QUIC owners and propagate the original error. Keep constructor ownership coherent if spawn_with_tcp has already acquired a task. No shim or new configuration.
findings.regression: Existing actual origin spawn/request positives cover ordinary acquisition; use a narrowly source-justified acquisition-error seam only if needed for a reachable causal test. Do not add constructor-mirror controls or claim this OS error was measured.

findings.title: Local aliases precede standard and external imports
findings.cause: All four modules place crate support aliases before std/external imports, contrary to the supplied import-group rule. Several operation paragraphs also join unrelated lookup/readiness/assertion operations.
findings.remedy: Move existing local aliases to the local group and manually group only actual touched flows. Preserve cfg declarations and natural domain module responsibilities. No arbitrary file-size split or layout tests.
findings.related: Same standards issue as existing A129, with new four-file scope.
